rows.title_full:
AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE PHILIPPINE ECOSYSTEM AND
NATURAL CAPITAL ACCOUNTING SYSTEM, MANDATING ITS
USE IN POLICY AND DECISION-MAKING, DESIGNATING THE
AGENCIES RESPONSIBLE FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION,
PROVIDING INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS AMONG
RESPONSIBLE AGENCIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS
THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Philippine Ecosystem And Natural Capital Accounting System ( P E N C A S) Act
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others as follows:  Ecosystem - refers to all living things in a given area, as well as their interactions with each other; and with their non-living environments (weather, earth, sun, soil, climate, atmosphere); Natural capital - refers to the stock of renewable and non-renewable resources, including plants, animals, air, water, soils, and minerals, that provide a flow of benefits to people.  It also includes ecosystem services such as air and water filtration, flood protection, carbon sequestration, pollination of crops, and habitats for wildlife.
Provides for PENCAS framework that shall include, among others, a list of officially designated statistics on the depletion, degradation, and restoration of natural capital; environmental protection expenditures; pollution and quality of land, air and water;  environmental damages; and genuine savings.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROMOTING THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE DOWNSTREAM NATURAL
GAS INDUSTRY, CONSOLIDATING FOR THE PURPOSE ALL LAWS RELATING TO THE
TRANSMISSION, DISTRIBUTION AND SUPPLY OF NATURAL GAS, AND
APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Philippine Downstream Natural Gas Industry Development Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to provide a framework for the development of the Philippine Downstream Natural Gas Industry (PDNGI) that would serve as a pillar towards achieving the rapid development of the country´s natural gas sector. Defines the responsibilities of various government agencies and private entities to achieve this national goal.
Provides for the following key provisions: 1.) the structure, operation and regulation of the Downstream Natural Gas Industry; 2.) transmission and distribution system and related facility; 3.) third-party access 4.) standards on product quality, facility, and safety practice 5.) responsibilities of the permit holder or operator 6.) incentives to PDNGI projects, as certified by the DOE 7.) promotion of competition; and 8.) fines and penalties to be imposed for the violation of the provisions of this Act.
Mandates the Department of Energy to be the lead agency responsible for the supervision and monitoring of the Industry and the regulation of the construction and operation of natural gas pipelines and related facilities for the transmission, distribution, and supply of natural gas.
Stipulates that the Energy Regulatory Commission shall have the sole regulatory responsibility for establishing the rates and related terms and conditions of service for the transmission and distribution, regasification and supply of natural gas.
rows.status: Republic Act RA12120 enacted on 2025-01-08

rows.author: K127;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING COURT OF MARITIME APPEALS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address issues, disputes, or claims surrounding the maritime industry which may involve complex jurisdictional issues in a globalized context - the resolution of which requires technical expertise in the field of maritime law.
Proposes that CMA shall be of the same level as the Court of Appeals - possessing all the inherent powers of a Court of Justice, and shall consist of a Presiding Justice and eight (8) Associate Justices”¦
Proposes that CMA shall exercise exclusive appellate jurisdiction to review by appeal - decisions on the following range of cases as follows:  seafarer´s money claims (NLRC); vessel registration fees, tonnage fees, accreditation fees, safety certificates, certificates of public convenience, licenses, special permits or other matters administered by the MARINA; maritime safety and maritime environment laws (Phil. Coast Guard); and all actions in admiralty and maritime jurisdiction originally decided or resolved (RTC) . . .
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2023-07-25

rows.author: K127;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2025-06-04, transmitted to the Senate on 2025-06-09 and received by the Senate on 2025-06-09
rows.title_full: UPGRADING AND STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE MARITIME INDUSTRY TO MEET THE STRATEGIC NEEDS OF THE CHANGING INTERNATIONAL AND DOMESTIC MARITIME INDUSTRY AND ADDRESS THE ECONOMIC AND NATIONAL MARITIME DEFENSE SITUATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to upgrade and modernize the curriculum of the Philippine Merchant Marine Academy (PMMA) to ensure the production of quality graduates who are responsive to the needs of the country. 
Intends to address the economic and defense requirements of the country including Naval, Maritime Law Enforcement, and other Maritime Trade and maritime education and training development in reference to UN-IMO STCW requirements.
Proposes that PMMA shall be engaged in the following academic areas:  Marine Transportation (Major in Ship Management and Minor in Maritime Cyber Security; Marine Engineering (Major in Communications, Electrical, and Minor in Maritime Software Development; Operational Level Assessment of MARINA; Ship Management and Maritime Education; Research & Development; world economic and shipping trends, etc.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11393

rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROMOTING INCLUSIVE EDUCATION, ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND
EMPLOYMENT FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AMONG 4Ps
ADULT BENEFICIARIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE
REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11310, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE
“PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps)”
rows.title_short:
Promoting Inclusive Education, Entrepreneurship And Employment For Sustainable Development Among 4 Ps Adult Beneficiaries, Amending For The Purpose
Republic Act No. 11310, Otherwise Known As The
“ Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4 Ps)”
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide Community Mobilization Grant of not lower than Five Hundred Pesos (P500.00) that shall be used to finance meals and transportation related to the availment of adult education per adult beneficiary of the adult education program.
Encourages at least one (1) adult beneficiary to join and complete any of the following tracks of adult education: 1.) non-formal education through the ALS track of the Department of Education 2.) entrepreneurship track of the Department of Trade and Industry and Department of Social Welfare and Development; and 3.) employment track of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority of their accredited private sector and civil society organizations.
Gives priority to adult education beneficiaries in the availment of the modalities and intervention of the government programs after the completion of their selected track of adult education.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-08-22, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-08-23 and received by the Senate on 2023-08-23
